public_rationale: Meta's announcement confirms that Muse Glimmer had downloadable weights on August 10. A preserved NYT headline uses ‘Open Source’, but the article body could not be read. These records support parts of Marcus's statement without establishing the complete accusation. The release classification also needs a dated inventory checked against the stated standard.
limitations: The NYT wording is evidenced through a secondary headline archive.
A permissive weights license alone does not settle whether the complete model release is open-source.
Failure to retrieve an artifact is not proof that it was never released.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Meta's newly released model is open-weight but not open-source, and the New York Times wrongly described it.

statement.excerpt: The new Meta model is open-weight but not open-source. NYT got it wrong.
statement.document_title: Open-source is NOT the same as open-weight

our_interpretation: Assess the release and coverage as they stood on August 10, 2026, the post date.
Identify the unnamed model from contemporaneous release records. The screens' identification of Muse Spark 1.2 is a research lead, not part of Marcus's words.
Use the Open Source Initiative's AI Definition 1.0 as an explicit reference standard, alongside Marcus's stated concern about access to the training pipeline.
The newspaper criticism requires evidence that the relevant NYT coverage described this model as open-source, rather than merely reporting someone else's terminology.
criteria.support_condition: The identified model had downloadable weights but lacked materials required by the stated open-source standard, and the relevant NYT coverage represented it as open-source.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The identified release met the stated open-source standard, did not have available weights, or the relevant NYT coverage expressly distinguished open weights from open source.
